My understanding is that: **Committee selection** - For each epoch, we take the set of active validators - Assign those validators to a committee of some size Y such that each committee has roughly the same size. - Then for each slot in the epoch we have N committees such that each slot has roughly the same number of committees. **Voting** - For each slot, a proposer proposes a block - The committees assigned to that slot vote on it. In total, we have N * Y signatures for the slot - The votes in each committee gets separately aggregated, so we then have N aggregated signatures per slot, one for each committee I think there was an EIP to allow us to aggregate the N * Y signatures into 1, and the issue was that each committee is signing over a slightly different message So everyone signs now but it’s msgs which differ per comitees? Yeah exactly -- the message is basically the same except that it includes the committee index, so we cannot aggregate over the whole slot Not all schemes allow efficient sig aggregation BLS is really an exception Schnorr etc are terrible at that So q is which pq scheme would be as efficient People say schnorr good for threshold while in reality it’s just orders of magn worse I think the closest thing to BLS would be lattice based or aggregation using the stark hammer This EIP removes the index: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7549 Have you seen any real benchmarks? excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
I think this would be the simplest and nicest design in theory.

My understanding is that:

**Committee selection**

- For each epoch, we take the set of active validators
-  Assign those validators to a committee of some size Y such that each committee has roughly the same size. 
- Then for each slot in the epoch we have N committees such that each slot has roughly the same number of committees.

**Voting**

- For each slot, a proposer proposes a block
-  The committees assigned to that slot vote on it. In total, we have N * Y signatures for the slot
- The votes in each committee gets separately aggregated, so we then have N aggregated signatures per slot, one for each committee

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: I think there was an EIP to allow us to aggregate the N * Y signatures into 1, and the issue was that each committee is signing over a slightly different message

excerpts.author: paulmillr
excerpts.content: So everyone signs now but it’s msgs which differ per comitees?

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Yeah exactly -- the message is basically the same except that it includes the committee index, so we cannot aggregate over the whole slot

excerpts.author: paulmillr
excerpts.content:
Not all schemes allow efficient sig aggregation

BLS is really an exception
Schnorr etc are terrible at that

So q is which pq scheme would be as efficient

excerpts.author: paulmillr
excerpts.content: People say schnorr good for threshold while in reality it’s just orders of magn worse

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: I think the closest thing to BLS would be lattice based or aggregation using the stark hammer

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: This EIP removes the index: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7549

excerpts.author: paulmillr
excerpts.content: Have you seen any real benchmarks? Are they production ready?

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
Currently we have benchmarks of how long it takes current known proving systems to do a certain amount of hashes, which roughly lets you know how efficient hash based signature schemes will be.

It would also be good to look into lattice constructions, just so we have the numbers there

excerpts.author: paulmillr
excerpts.content: But signing something is not aggregation?

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Yep exactly, you would need to aggregate it inside of a stark

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: So the committee signs using lets say some post quantum signature scheme, then the aggregators will create a stark that aggregates them together

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: If we want stuff like that then I think we should be looking for signing schemes that are Stark friendly?

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Yep exactly — or cheap enough given our constraints
